title: Features: Commerce turned on
summary: DJDL's Settings → Features right after Commerce was switched on: the six features in canonical order as feature rows, each with its own switches in a box under it and its requirements (Commerce needs ✓ Licensing; Cloud Sync needs ✓ Managed config and ✓ Sign-in), Commerce's fact in the status column (No storefront ready yet) with Set up a storefront, the Commerce group now in the sidebar, and an undo toast.
compare: Six feature rows in canonical order: Licensing, Managed config, Ship builds, Sign-in, Cloud Sync, Commerce (the kit's .feature-row: glyph, name at the card step, one sentence, requirements, status column, switch). Every switch on the page has one style (the brand accent with the same knob), so track colour and knob position say on or off; service colours stay on the tiles. On phone each switch is 44×24 (.switch.touch) and the row's label toggles it.

Commerce reads 'Needs ✓ Licensing' (the tick says it's on; no 'which is on'), and Licensing reads 'Needed by Commerce' with a link glyph; Cloud Sync names both of its requirements, each with its tick. Every requirement comes from tools/services.json, so the copy is generated, never hand-written per page.

When a requirement is off, the dependent's switch is disabled, the requirement shows a lock, and its status column says what to turn on first ('Turn on Licensing first'); the server refuses it too (commerce_requires_license). Drawn in commerce.features-blocked; a failed save in commerce.features-save-failed.

A feature's own switches sit in a sunken box under its text (.feature-subs): Minted tokens (read-only status: On, following DJDL's 1 approved token recipe), In-app updates and Package feeds under Ship builds, Customer portal under Sign-in. No feature has a separate settings page for these.

Commerce's fact shows in the status column: 'No storefront ready yet' (muted, dashed ring) and the link Set up a storefront to Storefronts' first-run (commerce.first-run). Once a storefront is live it reads 'Selling on App Store and Steam'.

The row just switched on is tinted in Commerce's green for a moment. Turning a service on is L0: the toast says 'Commerce is on for DJDL' and that Storefronts, Offers and Purchases are in the sidebar (the row already says no storefront is ready), with Undo first and Open Storefronts beside it, under the text. It never covers a switch: it is drawn at the page's end (.toasts.at-end), where it lands once the page scrolls the switched row above it.
The sidebar shows the Commerce group (Storefronts, Offers, Purchases) as soon as the switch saves; Settings is the active item in the sidebar foot.

The rule is said once, in a callout above the card (in the aside at wide): each switch saves on its own, and turning a feature off also turns off what needs it, after you confirm. Raw service names and the registration policy are only under Advanced, linked once in the card's foot.

Phone: each row keeps its tile, name and switch on the first line; the description, requirements and status wrap under the name; the nested box takes the full width; the toast spans the width at the page's end.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink and selection is ink, the accent marks context only; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.

Masthead mark (B4): from 1024px a 48px flat tile on this page (the feature's glyph on a landing page, the product's icon on a product page) replaces the orientation chip; below 1024 the chip carries the context; never on a dense data page, a record or a state page.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: the toast has Undo and never covers a switch, switches share one style, and the requirement-off and failed-save states are drawn.

findings.issue: [house rules] Turning a service on is L0 (an undo toast) but the toast has no Undo, and its one ghost action squeezes the message to four lines.
findings.resolution: Undo is the toast's first action (outline) with Open Storefronts beside it (ghost), both under the text.

findings.issue: [visual] The toast covers the Sign-in and Customer portal switches on desktop and In-app updates and Package feeds on phone, and in a real viewport would sit over the Commerce row.
findings.resolution: Desktop: the toast sits bottom right inside the 272px gutter beside the narrow page (244px wide), clear of every switch; the message runs four lines at that width rather than the suggested two, because a 360px toast can't fit the gutter without covering switches. Phone: drawn after the list, as when the page scrolls the switched row above it. Compare items 6 and 9 updated.

findings.issue: [plan / missing state] The owner rule (on only when requirements are on) isn't drawn, nor a failed save.
findings.resolution: Added commerce.features-blocked (Licensing and Sign-in off: Commerce and Cloud Sync switches disabled with aria-disabled, the line and tooltip 'Needs Licensing. Turn it on first.', Turn on Licensing / Turn on Sign-in links, no Commerce group in the sidebar) and commerce.features-save-failed (switch back off, an inline danger line with a reference id and Try again, no toast).

findings.issue: [visual] Each switch uses its service colour and the knob is black on some on-switches and white on others, so the knob no longer signals state; the kit switch is 36x20 on phone, below the 24px target.
findings.resolution: Every switch on the page (and on commerce.turn-off-licensing and the two new feature states) uses the brand accent with one knob style; service colours stay on the tiles. The 24px phone hit area is now a compare requirement (the row's label toggles the switch); the kit keeps drawing the 36x20 switch, since a hit area isn't visible in a picture.

findings.issue: The Commerce status breaks the toggle column; dependencies are told twice per row; banner is long; nested box; coloured row tint.
findings.resolution: Commerce's state is a meta line under its description so the switches share one x; 'Needs X' appears only on the dependent row and 'Needed by' is removed; banner is 'Each switch saves on its own.'; nested switches use row padding and a hairline; the just-on row has a neutral tint and the accent bar; dependency lines are 13px; the page is one column (no rail).
'Commerce turned on' with one action, Undo.

findings.issue: [wide 1920] Console pages stretch tables and attention rows across the whole width.
findings.resolution: Page content is capped at 1280px, left-aligned, from 1600px (.cm2 page cap); attention text is capped at 72ch with its action beside it.

findings.issue: Move the footer note about service names and the registration policy into Advanced.
findings.resolution: declined: Relocates content between screens, outside this pass.

findings.issue: Keep both Undo and Open Storefronts in the toast.
findings.resolution: declined: One action is enough; the sidebar already links to Storefronts.

findings.issue: Add breadcrumbs to Features, Purchases and Storefronts.
findings.resolution: declined: Breadcrumbs belong on detail pages only.
